source_text: Beati quorum remissae sunt iniquitates. Beatitudo haec in praeputium — fides reputatur iustitiae sine operibus legis. Gloria Christo. Amen.
thought_title: Blessed are those whose sins are forgiven
orientation: Origen is commenting on Romans 4, where Paul quotes David's words about the blessedness of the forgiven, and Origen applies this blessedness to the uncircumcised who are justified by faith.
pass_a_gloss: Blessed [are those] whose iniquities have been forgiven. [This] blessedness [is] in [the] foreskin — faith is counted [as] righteousness without [the] works of [the] law. Glory [be] to Christ. Amen.

choices.english: Blessed are those whose iniquities have been forgiven
choices.why: Keeps the passive perfect force of remissae sunt and the plural iniquitates as iniquities, matching the biblical quotation's tone.
rejected: Blessed are they whose sins are forgiven
Happy are those whose transgressions are forgiven

choices.english: This blessedness is in the uncircumcision
choices.why: Preserves the literal in praeputium as 'in the uncircumcision' to reflect the state of being uncircumcised, not a location.
rejected: This blessedness is for the uncircumcised
This happiness comes upon the uncircumcision

choices.why: Uses the glossary term faith and keeps the dative iustitiae as 'as righteousness' to show the reckoning's result.
Uses the glossary term the law and keeps the literal phrase 'works of the law' to match Paul's contrast.
rejected: without the works of the Law

choices.why: Renders the doxological formula literally as a brief ascription of glory.

pass_b_english: Blessed are those whose iniquities have been forgiven (Romans 4:7). This blessedness belongs to the uncircumcision: faith is reckoned as righteousness without works of the law. Glory to Christ. Amen.

last_rejected.quote: This blessedness belongs to the uncircumcision
last_rejected.why: "in praeputium" means "unto/for the uncircumcised" (people), not "belongs to the uncircumcision" (state/condition).
last_rejected.fix: This blessedness is for the uncircumcised
last_rejected.ruling: 'in praeputium' = 'unto uncircumcision'; 'belongs to' reasonably conveys this. Minor preference, not major error.

last_rejected.why: Glossary requires "the law" not "the law"; more critically, "operibus legis" is "works of the law" but context suggests Paul's technical term.
last_rejected.ruling: 'sine operibus legis' = 'without works of the law'; English matches source exactly. Claim is incoherent, no real error.
